title: LLMCompiler: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling (ICML 2024, project README)
event_hint: LLM compiler that plans and executes parallel function calls for tool-using LLMs
problem: Sequential ReAct-style reasoning-and-acting for each function call in multi-tool LLM agents creates high latency, high cost, and sometimes inaccurate behavior, because independently-callable functions are still executed one at a time.
mechanism: LLMCompiler decomposes a user request into tasks, and a Planner automatically identifies which function calls can run in parallel versus which are interdependent, then computes an optimized orchestration (a task DAG). A Task Fetching Unit resolves dependencies and an Executor dispatches parallel calls; streaming pipes tasks from the Planner to the Executor immediately as they are generated rather than blocking until the full plan is produced. Users supply tools plus optional in-context examples; the planner generalizes across open-source (LLaMA, vLLM-served, Friendli) and closed (OpenAI GPT, Azure) models.

evidence.claim: LLMCompiler identifies which tasks can be performed in parallel and which are interdependent, orchestrating multi-function calling automatically.
evidence.source_locator: README TL;DR: 'automatically identifying which tasks can be performed in parallel and which ones are interdependent'

evidence.claim: The user specifies tools with optional in-context examples and LLMCompiler computes an optimized orchestration for the function calls.
Streaming emits tasks from the Planner to the Task Fetching Unit and Executor immediately after generation, improving latency versus blocking until all tasks are generated.
Across tasks with different parallel-calling patterns, LLMCompiler demonstrated latency speedup, cost saving, and accuracy improvement.
evidence.source_locator: README TL;DR; baseline ReAct supported via --react flag

evidence.claim: Supported benchmarks are HotpotQA, Movie Recommendation, and ParallelQA; ReAct is provided as the baseline comparator.

evaluation_context: Benchmarks bundled in the repo: HotpotQA, Movie Recommendation (movie), ParallelQA. Baseline is ReAct. OpenAI GPT models used by default; custom models via vLLM and Friendli endpoints also supported; Azure endpoint supported. No specific speedup percentages, token counts, or hardware are given in the README.
limitations: This is the project README, not the ICML paper; it states that speedup/cost/accuracy gains occurred but gives no numeric magnitudes, confidence intervals, or model-specific breakdowns (those require the paper). Correctness/risk of speculative parallel execution (e.g., wasted calls when dependencies are mis-predicted) is not quantified here. Workloads are general function-calling QA tasks, not coding-agent Read/Grep tools, so direct transfer to code-search acceleration is an inference.
project_relevance: Core reference for the agent tool-chain parallel-execution question: it is the canonical method for running independent tool calls concurrently instead of sequentially, which is directly applicable to parallelizing a coding agent's independent Read/Grep/Glob calls. The Planner/Task-Fetching-Unit/Executor split and streaming are reusable design patterns for reducing agent end-to-end latency. Relevance to code-graph and speculative tool execution is high, though the repo does not evaluate coding-agent workloads.
source_notes: Document is the official GitHub README for SqueezeAILab/LLMCompiler (ICML 2024); primary source for the framework design and usage, but not for numeric evaluation results.
Authors per citation: Kim, Moon, Tabrizi, Lee, Mahoney, Keutzer, Gholami (arXiv 2023, ICML 2024).
Numeric latency/cost/accuracy figures are absent; consult the paper for magnitudes.
